newsitem.title: MEXICO: Leader of Mexico's PRI says no plans to quit.
newsitem.headline: Leader of Mexico's PRI says no plans to quit.

text.p: The president of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) Roque Villanueva on Tuesday ruled out stepping down, a little more than a week after a crushing blow for the party in mid-term elections.
When asked on television programme Hechos whether he would stay as party president, Villanueva said, "up to now that is the idea...."
He said the national council of the PRI "is not putting pressure for any change at the moment."
The PRI, which has ruled Mexico for 68 years, lost its majority in the lower house of Congress in the July 6 vote.

At the same time, the opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution captured the mayor's job in Mexico City, the country's nerve centre. The right-wing National Action Party also took two more state governorships from the PRI in the July 6 vote.
